newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower as recent buying halts.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower as recent buying halts.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed lower amid a lack of follow-through buying from the funds, which had carried the market to nearly three-week highs Thursday, traders said.
The market opened lower and remained under pressure by producer selling and the failure of the benchmark-March contract to pierce resistance at 10.70 cents, earlier in the week.
Traders cited stops above 10.70 cents, where additional short-covering is expected to emerge.
The March/May spread, which strengthened to 0.10 this week, closed at 0.06 cent. Trade selling narrowed the spread to 0.02 cent at one point during the session.
Open interest in the March contract stood at 56,731 lots as of Thursday's close, down 2,779 lots from the previous day, with three weeks remaining until the contract expires.
March settled down 0.06 at 10.60 cents, having ranged from 10.66 to 10.56. The back months closed 0.04 to 0.02 cent lower.
Volume was estimated at 13,637 lots compared with Thursday's official volume of 24,059 lots.
